sections.h2: Where is the Hertford County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Go to the third floor of the Hertford County Courthouse, 119 Justice Drive, Suite 9, in Winton. The office phone is 252-358-7850, and hours run from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM Monday through Friday except county holidays and closings.

The county says its staff maintain real estate documents going back as far as 1862. Winton became the county seat in 1766, and the county history page notes land deeds in the area dating to 1710. The office holds deeds, deeds of trust, maps, military discharge records, notary records, and birth, death and marriage records for events in Hertford County.

The county lies in the northeast corner of North Carolina against the Virginia line. Farming remains its economic backbone, with tobacco, cotton, peanuts, corn and soybeans listed as staples, and the Chowan River crosses its land. QuickFacts lists 353.16 square miles of land.

sections.h2: What does Hertford County post as its recording fees?
sections.html:
The county posts a fee schedule marked as subject to change. Cash, checks, money orders and cards are accepted, and checks should be payable to the Hertford County Register of Deeds with a working phone number on them. Documents returned by mail need a self-addressed stamped envelope.

Real estate lines from the Hertford County Register of Deeds fee schedule
ItemPosted charge
Deeds and general instruments$26.00, first 15 pages; $4.00 per extra page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64.00, first 35 pages; $4.00 per extra page
Excise tax on deeds$2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price
Satisfactions and cancellationsNo fee
Non-standard document$25.00 per document
Several instruments in one packet$10.00 extra

Uncertified copies run $.25 per page, plat copies $3.00 per page, and certified copies $5.00 for page one and $2.00 for each added page. Requests by fax or online carry their own charge of $1.00 for the first page and $.25 for each added page.

sections.h2: Which formatting rules can trigger the Hertford County nonstandard fee?
sections.html:
The county repeats the paper standards from G.S. 161-14 on its recording rules page. A document that misses them is still recorded, with the $25.00 nonstandard fee added.

  • Letter or legal size paper, one side only
  • Black type on white, 10 point or larger
  • Wide blank band across the head of page one

Hertford adds a drafter rule from Session Law 2011-351: no deed or deed of trust is accepted unless page one names the person or law firm that prepared it. The county also asks for the tax parcel pin on deeds, together with either a tax department stamp showing no delinquent taxes or the stock sentence that any delinquent taxes will be paid by the closing attorney to the county tax collector from closing proceeds. An electronic deed must carry that sentence.

sections.h2: Can a Hertford County deed be e-recorded?
sections.html:
Yes. The county's FAQ says it e-records every document except maps, and the e-recording page names two submitters, Corporation Service Company and Simplifile. Documents travel from the submitter's office to the register and the recorded copy returns electronically right after recording.

Your closing attorney picks the route. If you walk a paper deed to Winton instead, the office still needs a drafter name on page one and your return envelope if you want it mailed back.

sections.h2: What can the Hertford County office not do for a seller?
sections.html:
The list matters more than people expect, because sellers often call the register for help it cannot give.

  • It cannot search a title, because state law bars register staff from doing so. An individual or a legal representative can run the search.
  • It cannot confirm whether a lien exists. A deed of trust recorded in the office is the sign that the property secured a loan.
  • It cannot change a recorded deed. A new deed must be prepared, and the office recommends seeing an attorney.
  • It cannot name an owner from a street address, since records are indexed by name. Land Records Mapping, at 252-358-7809, handles location questions.
  • It holds no estate, will or divorce records. Those sit with the Clerk of Superior Court, 252-358-7100.

Real estate documents are available online, though older indexes and images may not be. A certified copy of a lost original deed costs the same $5.00 plus $2.00 per added page.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax in a Hertford County sale?
sections.html:
The seller, because G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor pay the register before the deed can be recorded. The county prints the rate as $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price, which matches the statute's dollar per five hundred. Half goes to the county and half to the Department of Revenue.

A conveyance only binds later purchasers and lien creditors from the time it is registered, per G.S. 47-18. Plan closing and recording for the same day. The statutes are at G.S. 105-228.30 and G.S. 47-18.

sections.h2: What else is handled at the Winton counter?
sections.html:
The same office issues licenses and certificates, and the fee schedule and FAQ list the details. Knowing them helps if a seller also needs paperwork for an estate or a move.

  • Marriage license: $60.00, issued from 8:30 AM until 4:30 PM, valid for sixty days. A couple can buy it in Hertford County and marry anywhere in North Carolina.
  • Magistrate wedding: $50.00, arranged through the magistrate at the sheriff's department.
  • Certified birth, death or marriage copy: $10.00 each, with a government photo ID. Only close relatives or an authorized agent can pick one up.
  • Online vital record requests: $3.50 added, through the county's Get Certificate Now program.
  • Notary oath: $10.00. The Secretary of State sends the notice and no appointment is needed.
  • Beer licenses: $5.00 off premises and $25.00 on premises. Wine licenses: $25.00.
  • Military discharge filing and certified copy: free, though discharges are not open to public viewing.

sections.h2: How small is the Hertford County housing market?
sections.html:
Population fell from 24,669 in 2010 to 21,552 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 19,015. There are 9,873 housing units, and only 3 building permits were issued in 2025.

  • Median home value among owners, 2020 to 2024: $119,200
  • Share of owner households: 67.4 percent
  • Rent at the midpoint: $844
  • Household income at the midpoint: $45,537
  • Seniors 65 or older: 27.1 percent

Values are modest, so a deed's recording fees and the excise tax take a larger bite of a small sale than they would elsewhere. Ask your closing attorney for the full list of closing costs before you commit to a price. Source: Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: How does the 2027 revaluation touch deeds recorded now?
sections.html:
The county's revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, the first since 2019, and field measuring began in July 2025. Deeds recorded before and after that date use the same recording steps. What changes is the assessed value attached to the parcel.

The Tax Assessor and Tax Collector offices are at 115 Justice Drive in Winton. The collector notes that real property is listed in the owner's name as of January 1, so ask the office about the current bill before you close. The county also warns the public about deed scams, with a fraud detection page linked from the Register of Deeds site.

faqs.q: How much does Hertford County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: Page one through fifteen of a general instrument cost $26.00 in total, with $4.00 for each added page. A deed of trust is $64.00 for its first 35 pages. The county says fees are subject to change, so call 252-358-7850 first.

faqs.q: What is the excise tax on a Hertford County deed?
faqs.a: The county lists $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price. That equals the state rate of one dollar per $500, and the seller pays it to the register before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What happens if my Hertford County deed is formatted wrong?
faqs.a: The office still records it and adds a $25.00 non-standard fee. Check paper size, margins, type size and the drafter's name beforehand to avoid the charge.

faqs.q: Can Hertford County staff search my title or find a lien?
faqs.a: No. State law prohibits register staff from searching titles, and the office cannot say whether a lien exists. Hire an attorney or title professional, who can read the recorded deeds of trust.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of my recorded deed in Hertford County?
faqs.a: Yes, in person or through the county sites, where real estate documents are online but older indexes and images may be missing. A certified copy costs $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page.
